newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs approve ONP voice telephone rules.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs approve ONP voice telephone rules.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday approved a proposal to update rules covering voice telephone service, which will be thrown open to competition in January 1998.

"(This) will be the most visible result of the ongoing liberalisation process of the telecommunications markets in Europe, and by far the one with the most direct consequence for all citizens in their daily life," the parliament said in a report drafted by British Socialist Mel Read.

This was the second time Euro-MPs had examined legislation to revise a 1995 directive -- 96/62/EC -- on the application of "open network provision" to voice telephony. The rules aim to ensure that phone users and competing phone companies have efficient and fair access to voice telecoms networks.
Parliament rejected the Council's first common position on the proposal because it did not include adequate commitments to universal service and consumer protection.
The new draft directive -- COM(96)419 -- addressed these weaknesses and won parliament's support in the first reading.
The economic and monetary committee recommended amendments to bring mobile phones within the scope of the directive, but they were rejected by a majority of Euro-MPs.
The European Commission had also argued mobile and fixed phones were two different markets and should be dealt with accordingly.
Parliament approved amendments to improve the directive's provisions on consumer protection and the financing of universal service, or affordable service to all residents.

Euro-MPs also called for provisions to prevent operators charging higher prices for services in rural areas, regular checks on the tariffs applied by member states, and publicly available phone directories.
They said people must be able to make free emergency calls from public pay phones using a standard EU number -- 112.
Other amendments introduced flexible pay schemes for low income households and guaranteed users would not be completely disconnected if they did not pay on time.
The draft directive needs the approval of both ministers and Euro-MPs to become law and concilitation talks may be needed to reach a compromise.
